parsed.explanation: Thin-data jurisdiction: no trans-specific criminal statute, but a public-morals offence with heavier-than-standard penalties, documented arrests on false accusations, and documented police mistreatment/torture of LGBTQ people with an entrenched discrimination climate and no anti-discrimination recourse. A trans visitor is assessed against documents as issued (no LGR), so any ID check or custody encounter risks outing into a hostile system. No organised sweeps or universal-exposure measures documented, but weak rule of law means society hostility is unremedied. Extrapolating from criminalisation-plus-abuse-plus-concealment, this sits high in the High Risk band.

entry_documents.exposure: Visitor assessed strictly against documents as issued; no legal gender recognition exists, so any document-presentation mismatch at entry could out the traveller to officials.
entry_documents.protection: No documented refusals of entry or screening rules targeting trans people.
entry_documents.interaction: An outing at the border feeds directly into a policing system with documented LGBTQ mistreatment.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Article 85 permits 6 months–2 years for public same-sex affection; arrests on false accusations documented; police mistreatment/torture of LGBTQ people documented; 2012 record of torture, rape and impunity by security forces; no data on trans detainee placement.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Weak rule of law converts any custody into serious exposure; complaints offer no realistic remedy.

federal_state_facilities.interaction: No facilities, bathhouse or ward-placement rules sourced for trans visitors.

care_services.exposure: No anti-discrimination law in healthcare; medication continuity undocumented; HRT import rules unsourced.
care_services.interaction: Discovery as trans in a care setting could compound discrimination documented against LGBTQ people generally.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: SOGI publicly framed as imported and contrary to local values; heavier penalties than comparable morals offences; community forced underground; police treated LGBTQ people abusively.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: UN joint statement signed; UPR recommendations received — paper-level only, no operative effect documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State framing licenses social hostility and police discretion.

minors_guardians.exposure: Aggravated penalties (2–5 years) where a participant is a child; a parent travelling with a minor faces no documented trans-specific rule, but any same-sex-read relationship is criminalised and custody conditions are harsh.
minors_guardians.interaction: Constitutional family/marriage protection offers nothing to a trans adult travelling with a minor.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Entrenched societal discrimination documented; relationships described as dangerous; 2023 report recorded no anti-LGBTQ violence but reporting absence is unresolved.
street_violence_police_response.protection: None documented; police are themselves documented abusers.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Victims conceal rather than report; impunity prevails.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination law; no known LGBT rights organisations until a single registered group; no functioning complaint recourse documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Data-protection law restricts processing of sexual-orientation data (gender identity unaddressed) — marginal at most.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Without remedies, any outing escalates unchecked.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar police extortion/abuse profile and weak recourse, but this jurisdiction's penalties (up to 2 years) and documented torture context are somewhat more severe than short shakedowns; slightly below that anchor's reassurance level, so above 0.25 is not warranted on severity.

Closest match: discretionary police action against gender/LGB-nonconforming people, release-or-fine outcomes, courts deferring to police, no lethal threat credibly documented. This dossier adds documented torture context and entrenched hostility, placing it at or slightly below this anchor.

Less bad than 0.45-A: no biometric universal-exposure registry and no documented pattern of detaining visitors; enforcement is sporadic and society conceals rather than the state surveils. That anchor's constant-verification exposure is absent here, so the score sits below it.

Less severe than 0.15-C: no morality-sweep unit, no coerced-confession pattern against visitors, capital clause absent, and 2012 recorded no arrests under the provision. Organised targeting tier is not documented.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is a single national system: a public-morals statute with enhanced penalties, sporadically enforced (no 2012 arrests; later arrests on false accusations), police documented as mistreating LGBTQ people within a broader record of torture and impunity, entrenched social hostility with concealment as the only strategy, no anti-discrimination or recognition machinery, and no functioning remedies. For a trans visitor, the main exposure is that any ID check, arrest, or medical encounter outs them into a system with no recourse and abusive police. No organised targeting or universal-exposure measure is documented, keeping this above the 0.15 tier; but criminalisation-plus-police-abuse-plus-hostile-society without remedies keeps it in the High Risk band, around 0.33.
